instruction.name: ldx.bu
instruction.description: ldx.bu indexed load from rj + rk.

cases.name: base operand through an ALU operation

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r4, $r0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r20'

./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r20, $r4'

experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; addi.d $r4, $r20, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r4, $r0; add.d $r4, $r4, $r20'
experiments.name: base operand path

latencies.notes: Latency from the base operand rj to the destination. The loaded value is turned back into an address with add.d (or add.d plus movfr2gr for the floating-point loads), and those helper cycles are subtracted.

cases.name: index/bound operand feeding the address directly

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r20, $r4'

cases.name: index/bound operand through an ALU operation

experiment.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r20, $r4; andi $r4, $r4, 7'

experiments.command: ./bench --method slope --unroll 800 --unroll2 1600 --iters 40 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; li.d $r22, -64; and $r20, $r20, $r22; li.d $r4, 8; st.b $r4, $r20, 0; li.d $r4, 0; st.b $r4, $r20, 8; li.d $r5, 0; li.d $r4, 0' --asm 'ldx.bu $r4, $r20, $r4'
experiments.name: index/bound operand path

latencies.notes: Latency from the index or bound operand rk to the destination. The loaded value is the operand itself, so no ALU step is needed; a second case puts andi/xori in the path, which adds one cycle.

throughput.name: 8 independent lanes
throughput.init: addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r4, $r0, 0; addi.d $r5, $r0, 8; addi.d $r6, $r0, 16; addi.d $r7, $r0, 24; addi.d $r8, $r0, 32; addi.d $r9, $r0, 40; addi.d $r10, $r0, 48; addi.d $r11, $r0, 56
throughput.command: ./bench --unroll 1000 --iters 1000 --warmup 10 --reps 5 --core 0 --init 'addi.d $r20, $sp, -1024; addi.d $r4, $r0, 0; addi.d $r5, $r0, 8; addi.d $r6, $r0, 16; addi.d $r7, $r0, 24; addi.d $r8, $r0, 32; addi.d $r9, $r0, 40; addi.d $r10, $r0, 48; addi.d $r11, $r0, 56' --asm 'ldx.bu $r12, $r20, $r4; ldx.bu $r13, $r20, $r5; ldx.bu $r14, $r20, $r6; ldx.bu $r15, $r20, $r7; ldx.bu $r16, $r20, $r8; ldx.bu $r17, $r20, $r9; ldx.bu $r18, $r20, $r10; ldx.bu $r19, $r20, $r11'

notes: Latency measured per source operand on LA464: base operand rj -> destination 5 cycles, index/bound operand rk -> destination 4 cycles when the loaded value feeds the address generation directly, and one cycle more when an ALU operation sits in the path. The 64-byte-aligned buffer holds 8 and 0 so the chase stays inside one cache line.
